interpretationFindings.finding: The frozen comparison has thirteen matching groups and two unresolved flags: Chhand 32 has ਹੈਂ/ਹੈ and Chhand 36 has ਰਫ਼ੀਕ/ਰਫੀਕ. These are verb-form and orthographic differences; neither is silently repaired or promoted to an adjudicated edition. The global 67-group caveat remains.

ਅਧੇ has contemplation-related and independent-support interpretations. For ਅਭੇ, the selected unfathomability reading follows the Punjabi commentary inspected by the author; absence of distinction or secrets and fear-related readings are recorded separately. The plainly distinct ਅਜੀਤ and ਅਭੀਤ remain separately explained.

ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ is explained through three worlds or three periods of time. Commentaries differ over the triad and relationship named by ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗ. Those possibilities are not combined into a falsely certain derivation; ਅਸਰਗ is not silently confused with ਸਵਰਗ.

ਅਨੀਲ has colourlessness and stainlessness readings; ਅਜੇ has unconquered and birthless readings. ਅਜਾਦਿ is explained through independence or priority/source in relation to Brahma. Each selected interpretation remains distinct from its alternative.

ਅਭਰਨ is materially disputed: independence from nourishment contrasts with ornament imagery, which the historical dictionary explicitly illustrates with Jaap. Its initial ਅ does not automatically prove a negative prefix. Both readings are recorded without changing the source.
ਅਗੰਜ, ਅਭੰਜ, ਅਝੂਝ and ਅਝੰਝ preserve different emphases of destruction, breaking, contest and disturbance. Divine invulnerability is not a promise that a reader cannot be harmed.

Depth and friendship stand beside freedom from entangling activity and bonds. The historical dictionary identifies ਅਮੀਕ as Arabic-derived and explicitly cites Jaap; its initial ਅ is not automatically a negative prefix. The frozen ਰਫ਼ੀਕ retains its ਫ਼ while the comparator uses ਫ. Neither a spelling repair nor avoidance of human responsibilities is implied.

ਨ੍ਰਿਬੂਝ and ਅਸੂਝ concern limits of understanding; ਅਕਾਲ concerns time or death. ਅਜਾਲ has a noose/entanglement reading alongside a steadiness rendering. These descriptions do not forbid study or promise bodily immortality.

The Allah reading of ਅਲਾਹ is distinguished from no-gain or unattainability interpretations. ਅਜਾਹ has locality and glory/unveiled interpretations. The Divine name is not used to suggest a different deity or to rank religious communities.

ਅਲੀਕ has boundary/mark-related, unknowability and affectionate readings. ਨ੍ਰਿਲੰਭ has independence and reach-related readings. ਅਸੰਭ has birthless and unmanifest explanations. The exact spellings remain frozen; unrelated dictionary senses such as falsehood are not substituted.

The identical ਅਭੂਤ ਹੈਂ occurrence appears in both chhands. Its main reading should remain consistent while alternatives are documented. Traditional element language is philosophical vocabulary, not modern chemistry or a claim that the Divine does not exist.

ਅਛੂਤ describes the Divine beyond material touch. The historical dictionary expressly distinguishes this Jaap usage from caste exclusion. The teaching must not classify any person as spiritually inferior because of birth or physical contact.

The draft distinguishes invisibility, freedom from sorrow, freedom from karmic or ritual constraint, and absence of delusion. ਅਕਰਮ does not mean an inability to act, and ਅਸੋਕ is not a prohibition on human grief.

The recurring ਅਜੀਤ and ਅਭੀਤ retain their unconquered and fearless senses. In Chhand 42, steadiness in ਅਬਾਹ and unfathomability in ਅਗਾਹ add separate qualities rather than making all four words interchangeable.

The Jaap dictionary citation supports immeasurability for ਅਮਾਨ. ਨਿਧਾਨ retains treasury imagery. The contrast between ਅਨੇਕ and ਫਿਰਿ ਏਕ holds multiplicity with oneness; the source does not require a sequence in which several deities later become one.

The Bhujang Prayat heading is separate from the four source records. The last record contains two epithets, ਅਭੇਖੀ and ਅਭੇਵੇ, and both need explanation. The latter has distinction-free and secret-free or unconcealed readings. An unknowability rendering from another context is not silently imported here.

ਕਾਲ ਕਾਲੇ is read beside care for all. ਗਉਣੇ and ਭਉਣੇ retain the paired movement/dwelling imagery of pervasion. Their frozen ਣ spellings are preserved rather than replaced with the ਨ forms found in Chhand 22.

contentFindings: No remaining content or bilingual grammar blocker was identified within the source-bound draft scope. This finding does not certify a canonical translation or settle the recorded lexical alternatives.

Chhand 31.02 selected unfathomability is attributed to the author-inspected Rampur Khera Punjabi passage; Neki fearlessness and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived distinction/secret-free readings remain visible rather than being combined as one meaning.
Chhand 34.04 records the materially different nourishment and ornament readings. The Mahan Kosh Jaap citation supports ornament as a real alternative; no initial ਅ prefix rule is assumed.
The exact ਅਭੂਤ source records at 34.03 and 40.03 use identical main bilingual explanations, with unit-specific nuance allowed.

Chhand 40.04 treats touch as a description of the Divine, not a caste status, and explicitly rejects caste exclusion. Human fear, grief, duties and bodily vulnerability are not mislabeled as spiritual failure.
Chhand 44 explains both epithets in its final record, keeps the heading separate, and limits the alternative readings to those supported in that actual context.
